newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus not excluding Murdoch deal.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus not excluding Murdoch deal.

text.p: French pay television group Canal Plus is fully focused on making its merger with Nethold work, but it has not ruled out working with media mogul Rupert Murdoch, its chairman said on Tuesday.
"I have never said that it was impossible to work with Murdoch. There are possibilities we will work together with Murdoch," chairman Pierre Lescure told an industry conference.
He said he appreciated the boundless energy of Murdoch and the professionalism of his team at British-based BSkyB but did not envisage any broad partnership.

"We are now working on the wedding with Nethold...I do not think there is room for another partner," said Lescure, who told the conference he had only joined forces with the Dutch-based media group after being betrayed by Germany's Bertelsmann,

Lescure predicted Murdoch would not launch his BSkyB satellite TV service in the French market because "he understands that there is no room for competition between two premium channels, BSkyB and Canal Plus."
Richard Dunn, excutive director of Murdoch's News International Television told the same conference that his group would "work with Canal Plus in some areas and be fierce rivals in others."

"We have not betrayed anybody," Lescure said. "It is clear that if Bertelsmann, our best friend in Germany, had not decided to remarry behind our back with CLT, we would not have started our moves to merge with Nethold."
Canal Plus, Havas, BSkyB and Bertelsmann in March of this year announced an ambitious deal to launch digital satellite television in Germany, Europe's biggest television market.

But the deal faltered when Murdoch got angry about Bertelsmann's lack of commitment and fell apart after the German company decided in April to merge its television interests with CLT of Luxembourg. Last month, Bertelsmann dropped its digital television plans saying they were too expensive.

Lescure said the Canal Plus merger deal with Nethold, controlled by Swiss-South African Richemont, was negotiated in some 18 days during which Nethold's Johann Rupert met all Canal Plus' main shareholders.
"We have not decided on some kind of territorial deal (with Nethold). It's a merger of quality and complementarity," he said, adding that only in Poland was there some overlap.
In Germany, he said the winner of the digital television battle was Bavarian media tycoon Leo Kirch.

"Kirch has won. But I am not sure whether he has today the financial backing to honour all his commitments, in Germany concerning companies that make the decoders, in Italy where he continues to have 45 percent of Telepiu...and a lot of other investments," Lescure said.
"Kirch is a bit like Murdoch, things happen so quicky that the banks have to run after him to keep up. He is going to have financing problems," Lescure predicted.

"As far as Murdoch is concerned, he is a man who is active in 25 battle fields at the same time, has never been known to appreciate nuances, walks on the feet of others and bursts open doors that are only slightly ajar," he said.
"He wants to impose himself in Germany and he will pay up to 49 percent of the financing of Leo Kirch if the latter takes him to Italy and Spain," Lescure said.
"Before the end of 1996, there will undoubtedly be new episodes in the billiards game with Germany, Italy and Spain."
